FIND: The `finding_by_id` dictionary comprehension in `build_feedback_records` uses a last-wins mapping (`{f.finding_id: f for f in findings}`). If multiple models submit findings with the same `finding_id` in a single round, only the last finding is retained.
FOLLOW: Downstream, when processing `cell_verdicts`, `admissibility_failures`, `duplicate_pairs`, and `rk_validation`, the code looks up the finding by `fid`. Because earlier findings with the same ID were dropped, their feedback is either lost entirely (if `rk_validation` checks `model_id` and fails to match) or mis-routed to the model that submitted the last finding. This causes silent evidence loss and breaks the corrective feedback loop for those models.
ANALYSE: HARD constraint violation. The operational directive §17 mandates that models receive feedback on their findings. Dropping findings due to ID collisions violates this requirement and corrupts the feedback channel. CONFIRMED.
